evidence.finding: timing-7 partial trace: first-pass source loop lines 38-52 is the top region (564 instructions, instruction_time_sum 29.18us, wait_instruction_time_sum 20.75us). VECTOR productive_ratio 0.432, wait_only_ratio 0.222, idle_ratio 0.346; SCALAR productive 0.112, wait_only 0.421, idle 0.467; MTE2 productive 0.217, idle 0.783. Explicit WAIT/BAR instructions are attributed to the Welford lines 48-50 (top WAIT_FLAG 2.12us, BARs 1.4-2.3us each). This localizes attention to the per-tile Welford update, but absolute_time_qualified=false, so these fractions are not full-device time and do not prove a dependency stall.

Candidate timing-7 kernel: Task Duration 85.92us, Block Dim 64, per-block aiv_time 41.70us; aiv_vec_time 17.50us (vec_ratio 0.420), aiv_mte2_time 14.84us (ratio 0.356, active BW 16.46GB/s), aiv_mte3_time 4.86us, aiv_scalar_time 10.50us, aiv_scalar_wait_time 21.60us, aiv_scalar_mte2_stall 9.06us, ResourceConflict vec_wait_ratio 0.487. Reference BatchNormV3: Task Duration 21.64us, Block Dim 32, per-block aiv_time 19.46us, aiv_vec_time 11.17us, aiv_mte2_time 8.58us at 58.27GB/s. Candidate is 2.27x per-block aiv time and 3.5x lower MTE2 bandwidth; 64 blocks need two 32-core waves while the reference needs one.

Compiled target IR for BLOCK_M=8, BLOCK_N=128, batch_dim=8, spatial_dim=4096: first loop runs 32 n_steps per program. Each tile executes a vector divf (arith.divf %new_mean, %new_mean_61), two vector subf, two mul/add pairs and two arith.select for mean/var, plus extui/add for cnt (lines 79-90). This confirms the per-tile Welford update contains an avoidable vector divide and redundant select/sub forms, and that the loop is elementwise/dependency-chained rather than a reduction.

Retained best source ca3ff529 passes all 27 formal cases; geo_mean 1.196. timing-7 is worst at 0.3526 speedup (81.85us vs 28.86us CANN), timing-8 0.4189, timing-1/2/4/5 about 0.79-0.84. Large fp32 shapes are the loss leaders, matching the two-wave 64-block profile.

hypothesis: The first-pass per-tile online Welford update is latency-limited by per-tile vector work in a 32-iteration dependency chain, not by MTE2 bandwidth (MTE2 is only 0.356 active with 16.46GB/s, while VECTOR/SCALAR show wait and the WAIT/BAR instructions sit on the Welford lines). Re-expressing the same Welford recurrence in delta form with a scalar reciprocal multiply (mean += delta*inv_step; var += delta*delta*(1-inv_step); one mask select on delta) removes one vector divide, one vector subtract and one vector select per tile while preserving Welford numerics, masks and element ordering.
change: In batch_norm_with_update_kernel first loop, replace (curr_input - mean)/step, the two tl.where selects and the separate new_var expression with delta = tl.where(mask, curr_input - mean, 0.0), new_mean = mean + delta * inv_step, new_var = var + delta * delta * (1 - inv_step), where inv_step is a scalar 1.0/step; keep cnt accumulation and all later mean/variance/normalization semantics unchanged.
expected: Per-block aiv_vec_time below 17.5us and Task Duration below 85.9us for timing-7; formal timing-7 speedup above 0.3526 with all correctness cases still passing; no change to host allocation, layout or special-case semantics.
validation: Preflight compile via the bridge, then host formal evaluation of all 27 cases with per-case speedups and correctness; compare candidate per-block aiv_vec_time, aiv_time, Task Duration and vec/mte ratios against current-profiling.
alternatives: Two-moment sum/sumsq accumulation (sum += x; sumsq += x*x) would cut vector ops further but changes rounding versus Welford and risks cancellation on large-mean cases; rejected to preserve established numerical behavior across all 27 cases.

Increase BLOCK_N (e.g. 512) to shrink iterations/barriers and enlarge MTE2 transfers; potentially larger effect but overrides autotune/layout for every shape and raises UB pressure, so deferred to a separate hypothesis.

Pair two feature channels per program to reduce grid 64->32 and remove the second 32-core wave; per-block work doubles so the arithmetic gain is small and indexing complexity is high; not selected this round.
discriminating_observation: If the vector-divide/select overhead in the Welford tile is the mechanism, the revised kernel should lower per-block aiv_vec_time and aiv_vec_ratio and shorten Task Duration while MTE2 active bandwidth remains near 16.5GB/s and the first-pass region's wait time falls. If MTE2 transfer inefficiency were binding, vec_time would not drop and duration would track MTE2 time instead.
